Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Alex: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in just a sec. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this deal. With me Samir and Becky from our SE team, Jordan's on the call for Success.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks. We have limited time, we want to focus on the anchoring approach and how egress is managed, and also the bench scope.
[00:27] Alex: Great. High level agenda, quick context from Alder, our proposed anchored VPC fabric options (peering vs interface endpoints/PrivateLink), sizing and bench plan, success criteria and timeline, then action items. Anything to add?
[00:41] Liam: Security will want to deep dive on key management and audit logs — we also have residency constraints (eu-west-1 for patient PII processing).
[00:50] Samir: Noted. We'll make sure to call out KMS integration and how logs flow to your SIEM, and region pinning.
[01:03] Nina: Quick context — we're migrating inference from an internal cluster that is 3 racks, about 200 concurrent requests at peak, with mixed short and long flows. Current latency p95 is about 140ms for short flows, cost is opaque. We're aiming to reduce latency to <60ms p95 and cut unit cost roughly in half.
[01:22] Becky: When you say mixed, can you give proportions?
[01:26] Carlos: Roughly 70% short chat-ish completions (<=256 tokens), 20% embeddings/rerank, 10% long generation (2k tokens for summaries).
[01:36] Alex: Perfect. That shapes the bench. Samir, can you walk through the anchored VPC options?
[01:40] Samir: Sure. Two main patterns we propose: one, VPC peering with static route for the inference subnets; two, interface endpoints / PrivateLink where requests go to an ENI backed endpoint in the customer's VPC and traffic stays inside the cloud. Both keep egress bounded but have tradeoffs: peering is simpler for bulk throughput and lower latency, PrivateLink gives tighter control and works better with overlapping CIDRs. For Alder's multi-region requirement we can place serving nodes in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 and route by region.
[02:17] Priya: Overlapping CIDRs are a thing for us, we have some legacy ranges that collide. PrivateLink sounds safer. What about cost delta?
[02:25] Samir: PrivateLink has per-GB and per-hour endpoint charge, and also may add a small hop that can increase p95 by ~5-12ms in our experience. Peering avoids that but requires non-overlapping CIDR or a NAT/translation layer.
[02:40] Liam: How do you handle egress to third-party telemetry or to S3 for logs? We need deny-by-default with explicit egress allow list.
[02:51] Becky: In the anchored pattern we can configure a proxy egress point in your VPC that accepts only permitted flows. Redwood Private control plane can be configured to route logs to your S3 via VPC endpoint; we also integrate with your KMS for envelope keys — though cust keys depend on your setup.
[03:10] Carlos: Any difference in required firewall rules?
[03:13] Samir: For peering you'll open the specific subnets; for PrivateLink you'll need the NLB security groups and the endpoint policy. We'll share example security group templates.
[03:28] Alex: OK let's talk success criteria — what does Alder need to see to sign off on a POC? Priya?
[03:34] Priya: We need: 1) region-locked inference only in eu-west-1 for EU PII flows, 2) p95 latency <60ms for short completions on eu-west-1, 3) deterministic egress controls with audit logs showing no outbound to internet except allowed domains, 4) workload sizing guidance that we can use for committed capacity, and 5) a plan to validate cost per 1k tokens.
[03:55] Alex: Good set. We'll map bench scenarios to those. Samir, bench plan details?
[04:00] Samir: Proposed bench: Phase A (2 days) — connectivity/latency microbench: 1k concurrent short requests (<=256 tokens) from a client in eu-west-1 through PrivateLink and through peering (if possible) to measure p50/p95/p99. Phase B (3 days) — mixed workload throughput: ramp to sustained 5k rps with mixed short/embedding/long patterns to exercise batching and KV cash (cache) hot paths. Phase C (2 days) — egress and security: simulate log flows, validate KMS integration, check audit trails. We'll provide runner scripts and the scaled-benchmarks spreadsheet with exact payloads.
[04:46] Nina: Question - for Phase B you said 5k rps, our current is 200 concurrent, what's the expected concurrency mapping?
[04:55] Samir: For short flows, 5k rps maps to a concurrency of roughly 1500 depending on token lengths and batching. We'll size the GPUs accordingly — recommend a mix of q4_0 quantized models and a fallback float config for long flows.
[05:10] Priya: We need recommended instance types. Also, can you commit to a test window or will your hosted nodes interfere with other customers?
[05:20] Becky: For the POC we can reserve dedicated nodes in the region and pin them to Alder's project to avoid noisy neighbors — that's part of Redwood Dedicated. If you prefer the anchored VPC fabric, the serving nodes still live in our managed infra but we provision dedicated capacity for the POC period.
[05:38] Liam: How about data residency — will any tokenization or telemetry leave eu-west-1?
[05:44] Samir: Tokenization happens at the serving node; if the serving node is in eu-west-1 then all inference data stays there. Control plane metadata might hit our control plane, but we can obfuscate sensitive fields and support a private control plane for Private deployments. We'll outline which metadata elements go to control plane.
[06:05] Priya: We will need an on-prem style private control plane for audit reasons if we go to production, but for POC cloud-hosted is fine as long as raw PII doesn't leave region.
[06:17] Alex: Noted. Next, timeline — recommended 2-week prep, 2-week bench/pilot, then sign off. Priya, what timeline are you targeting?
[06:26] Priya: We'd like to run the POC in May, ideally start week of May 10th and finish by May 28th before our budget review.
[06:34] Alex: That aligns; we'll aim to have the runbook and infra template to you by 4/8, and schedule bench the week of 5/11.
[06:43] Carlos: For metrics, what exact probes will you provide? We need token-level cost, p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates.
[06:53] Samir: We'll enable token accounting per request, and provide the per-token cost sheet. We'll also stream logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver via VPC endpoint. Some fields may be approximated due to internal aggregation but we'll provide raw request logs for the POC.
[07:10] Liam: On the security front, can you show SOC2 reports and do a quick walkthrough of your key rotation policy?
[07:16] Becky: Yes. We'll send our SOC2 Type II and ISO references after the call. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and we can rotate keys per your cadence. We'll also walk through audit log retention.
[07:31] Priya: Can you demonstrate the deny-by-default egress during the bench? We're trying to avoid any surprise telemetry egress.
[07:38] Samir: Absolutely — Phase C includes a hard egress policy validated by packet captures and audit logs. We'll provide the egress allow-list template.
[07:49] Alex: A few gotchas: if you pick peering, remember cross-region peering can add complexity; PrivateLink will make overlapping CIDRs easier. Also the KV cache warm-up behavior can affect p95 early in runs.
[08:03] Carlos: On KV cache, how do you recommend warming? We have small warm-up windows in our CI.
[08:08] Samir: We recommend a 20–30 minute warm-up with synthetic traffic representing typical prefixes — we'll share warm-up scripts. Also prefix caching can be persisted between runs for the POC if you want sustained perf.
[08:22] Nina: For the benchmarking sheet, can you include a column for expected cost delta versus our current infra? We need ballpark numbers for the budget review.
[08:31] Alex: We'll include an estimated per-1k-token cost and a modeled monthly bill based on your expected usage. It's an estimate but directional.
[08:39] Priya: Regarding commitments, if POC shows results we may want to fast-track Dedicated for the production rollout. What's the typical lead time?
[08:47] Becky: Dedicated capacity lead time depends on region and GPU type; typically 2–4 weeks once contract and sizing are agreed. For some common instance types we can provision faster.
[08:58] Liam: One more: how do you ensure no control plane telemetry includes PII? We need a list of control plane fields.
[09:05] Samir: We'll publish a control-plane telemetry map — request IDs, timestamps, performance metrics, but we avoid payload content. We'll redact or hash request payload identifiers when requested.
[09:17] Alex: Let's capture the explicit POC success criteria to be included in the scope doc. I'll read them back quickly: region-locked inference in eu-west-1 for EU PII flows; p95 <60ms on short flows; deny-by-default egress with audit logs proving no outbound to internet except allow list; workload sizing recommendation and cost per 1k tokens. Anything to add?
[09:38] Priya: Add: demonstration of KMS CMEK integration and a mini run showing key rotation without downtime.
[09:45] Alex: Noted.
[09:47] [10:00] (background cross talk)
[10:12] Samir: A few practical notes on testing topology: if we test PrivateLink, you'll need to create an interface endpoint and allow traffic from your app subnets; we'll give the NLB DNS and SGs. For peering, we'll want the peer VPC ID and routes.
[10:33] Priya: We'll gather that. Also our compliance team may want a short security review meeting — could you attend?
[10:39] Jordan: Yep, we can set that up. I'll coordinate with Becky and Samir to join the security deep dive.
[10:47] Nina: Bench specifics — payload sizes for short flows? Do you have sample prompts?
[10:53] Samir: We'll use representative prompts you provide plus synthetic variations; typical short flow payload around 120 tokens. Embedding workload will be 512-dim vectors typical embed size.
[11:03] Carlos: For long flows, you said fallback to float32 — that will increase cost, can you quantify during bench?
[11:10] Becky: Yes, Phase B will include a cost breakdown per-mode — quantized vs float fallback. We'll show per-token cost and an aggregated monthly estimate.
[11:22] Priya: About observability retention — we only need 30 days for POC but production might need 13 months. Will that change egress behavior?
[11:29] Samir: Not necessarily; logs can be forwarded to your long-term S3 in-region via a VPC endpoint, so nothing leaves region.
[11:36] Alex: Anything else from Alder before we wrap?
[11:39] Liam: One last: do you have any known limits around concurrent KV cache entries or sequence length? We saw some vendors throttle at 4k tokens.
[11:47] Samir: Our runtime supports up to 8k sequences in the stacks we plan to use; we'll note sequences and the recommended max to avoid degraded perf. The long generation fallback can be handled by a different model flavor if you need >8k.
[12:05] Priya: OK good. Let's talk schedule and handoffs. We'll share CIDRs by 4/7, you share runbook by 4/8, Samir sends bench scripts by 4/9 and we'll target bench week of 5/11. Security review 4/12.
[12:23] Alex: I'll send a calendar invite for the 4/12 security deep dive. Jordan will own that. Any blockers we haven't captured?
[12:30] Carlos: No blockers beyond CIDRs and compliance checklist.
[12:33] Alex: Great. Quick recap of next steps and owners — Alex will send scope doc and runbook; Samir will prep sizing and bench scripts; Priya will send CIDRs; Jordan will schedule security deep dive.
[12:46] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[12:48] Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Meeting ends.
